FBI says Artex AI open-source hacking tool used to breach networks in ‘under three hours’

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the FBI is warning that hackers are relying on autonomous AI hacking tools to launch cyberattacks across the U.S.
  • In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory, the FBI notes hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open-source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks.
  • Industry observers note that artex is one of several open-source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the FBI is warning that hackers are relying on autonomous AI hacking tools to launch cyberattacks across the U.S. and globally. The campaigns include a widespread hack of customers of American IT firm ConnectWise and across South Korea’s financial industry.

In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory, the FBI notes hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open-source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks.

Industry observers note that artex is one of several open-source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open-source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI claims Artex intrusions can be “noisy,” meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company’s defensive alerts. But the tools allow hackers to move at speeds that makes it far more harder for human defenders to keep up.

In some cases, Artex-linked attacks can move from targeting a system to active compromise “in under three hours.”.

The FBI’s warning comes as AI-powered hacks are escalating, particularly by finding easy-to-find security flaws and breaking into companies with relative ease.

According to recent reports, oftentimes, Artex will rely on rapidly scanning a victim’s network to look for signs of weakness, and then exploit simple security bugs, such as weak protections and exposed or stolen passwords to gain a foothold. From there, Artex allows the hacker to spread across the network for databases, mailboxes, and other sensitive information.

In a recent development, the FBI’s advisory noted that Artex has been used in several cyberattacks since the tool’s first public debut in July. Artex was used to hack a number of South Korean financial institutions, blamed in large part on weak cybersecurity defenses and lacking protections, such as multi-factor authentication. The attacks allowed hackers to steal the personal data of at least 68,000 people.

The FBI confirmed earlier findings from Microsoft that hackers also used Artex to break into IT management giant ConnectWise and gain access to the Microsoft 365 cloud environments of at least 2,250 of its customers.

The hackers, who Microsoft says are likely Chinese, used the tool to steal data from affected ConnectWise customers.

A spokesperson for ConnectWise did not respond to a request for comment about the FBI’s claim.

Cybersecurity company Barracuda also disclosed that it was breached as part of an Artex-linked attack by financially motivated criminals, in which the tool found an exposed credential belonging to a third-party service that Barracuda had not revoked when it ended work with the vendor. That access allowed the hackers to access stores of credentials used by Barracuda to collect data from its customers’ systems. Barracuda said it couldn’t rule out access, as its logs were not detailed enough, and chose to “assume the worst” and changed all of its customer credentials.

“Defenders who rely on spotting malicious activity and then responding to it will often arrive after the attacker has finished,” wrote Barracuda’s chief information security officer Arve Kjoelen.

A spokesperson for Barracuda told TechCrunch that the manufacturer “directly notified and advised a minority of XDR customers to revoke and recreate integration credentials,” but did not specify how many customers.

According to recent reports, after Artex was used in cyberattacks, the tool’s developer made the software closed-source to prevent further attacks. But the FBI indicates the previous open-source version continues to circulate and remains “widely accessible” for use in cyberattacks.

It’s not only companies and targeted victims that have been compromised as a result of weakened security exploited by AI tools; the tools themselves have been exposed as well, potentially allowing outsiders to access powerful hacking capabilities. Last week, researchers found hundreds of publicly exposed Artex systems online, which had been placed on the internet without a password, likely by mistake or misconfiguration — including the Artex system that was used to target South Korea.

Updated with response from Barracuda.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The app will become even more of a shopping mall, just in time for Black Friday.
  • Sources indicate that meta has a fresh gift for Instagram creators just in time for Black Friday and the holiday shopping season.
  • US creators who are also in Amazon's influencer program will now be able to add dozens of affiliate links directly to their Reels and Instagram posts, Meta declared.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The app will become even more of a shopping mall, just in time for Black Friday.

Sources indicate that meta has a fresh gift for Instagram creators just in time for Black Friday and the holiday shopping season. The organization is making it easier for influencers to promote Amazon affiliate products directly in their posts without having to rely on a link in bio service.

US creators who are also in Amazon's influencer program will now be able to add dozens of affiliate links directly to their Reels and Instagram posts, Meta declared. The links will take viewers directly to the Amazon app and creators will earn their usual commission from any purchase made via their content.

Instagram has enabled product tagging and shoppable posts for some time. But the manufacturer previously required that tagged products in Reels already exist in Meta's commerce catalog. Now, creators can instead link their Amazon account directly to Instagram and add up to 30 products in a single video (there's a 20-product limit for feed posts). The Instagram app will also show creators what commission to expect for each item.

Recent findings suggest that for creators, the timing of the new feature is particularly good. Commission from affiliate links is a central part of how many Instagram influencers earn money from their accounts. And posts with products linked directly can generate twice as many clicks as bio links, according to Meta. And while the tech giant won't take a cut of creators' commissions, these links are no doubt a valuable source of data to Meta about what their users are interested in.

Industry observers note that the update is the latest way Meta has made it easier for Instagram influencers to direct customers off-platform. The firm has also started allowing creators to add clickable links to captions and Reels if they pay for certain Meta One subscription looks. Those paid tiers also come with expanded link pages. Up to now, the company's restrictions on link-sharing have led many creators to depend on separate "link in bio" services. Now, it seems Meta is increasingly interested in offering those tools to creators directly.

It has been revealed that for now, Amazon affiliate linking is only available to creators in the United States who have a professional account on Instagram and are 18 or older. The company hasn't stated if it intends to expand the feature to creators in more countries.

Apple is working on a face unlock feature for the iPhone Duo that uses the front-facing camera for authentication, and it’s already testing it with the new iOS 27.3 beta released today, as reported by MacRumors. Presently, the only way to unlock the iPhone Duo is by using Touch ID or entering a passcode, which might feel like a step back if you prefer face authentication using the Face ID feature available on other iPhones.

The iPhone Duo’s face unlock feature seemingly has a few caveats, however: it’s only available for the lock screen, you can only use your face for an unlock if you have used Touch ID or input a passcode within 45 minutes, and you can’t use the face authentication for Apple Pay purchases.

iOS 27.3 is set to launch publicly in December, Apple said last month, so should the feature make it to the full release, you may not have to wait too long for it to be officially available.

US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10.
  • Wisconsin health officials mentioned the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child.
  • Industry observers note that for all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they’re the first deaths in decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania, one in Upcoming York, and one in Wisconsin.

Wisconsin health officials mentioned the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania’s health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state’s seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County, but state health officials have not confirmed it.

Industry observers note that for all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they’re the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania’s case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650.

With outbreaks that have been smoldering and flaring since last year, the US has reportedly lost its measles elimination status—as medical and public health experts have widely expected it would. A panel of experts for the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a regional branch of the World Health Organization, convened last week to review US measles data and assess its elimination status. The PAHO is set to announce its conclusion and the review’s other findings on Tuesday, November 17. But sources broke the news to The Wall Street Journal on Friday that the panel had found that the US had indeed lost its status.

Recent findings suggest that an elimination status is determined by international health authorities after a country has gone more than 12 months without continuous spread of a virus. The status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data indicate that a chain of transmission involving a viral strain with an identical genotype and lineage has continued uninterrupted for 12 months or longer.

The US earned its elimination status in 2000 after hard-fought vaccination campaigns over several decades. But US vaccination rates have slipped below protective levels in recent years, fueled by the rise of anti-vaccine rhetoric and vaccine misinformation from fierce anti-vaccine advocates, including current US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. As vaccination rates slipped, measles cases skyrocketed. The current case tally is the highest seen since 1991.

In a recent development, in reporting the PAHO’s determination, the Journal quoted Noel Brewer, chair of an independent US committee who presented findings about the country’s measles outbreaks to PAHO, on the country’s lamentable status: “Runaway measles outbreaks in the United States, as well as the needless deaths, are all due to low measles vaccination coverage. We’ve gotten comfortable letting children be stopped by a deadly disease and die from it.”.

The US Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to requests to comment about the loss of the elimination status or to answer a question about how anti-vaccine rhetoric and misinformation, including that from Kennedy, has contributed.

Medical and public health experts continue to sharply criticize Kennedy’s and the Trump administration’s poor handling of the ongoing severe outbreaks. The CDC has not held press briefings in efforts to halt the vaccine-preventable illness and promote vaccination. Instead, Kennedy reportedly ordered the CDC to remove measles death data, and the CDC director declined to approve an urgent health alert about the life-threatening risks of measles during pregnancy.

Microsoft outage cause revealed: It was a perfect storm of problems

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week.
  • Aside from wondering when their email would be working again, the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long?
  • In a statement shared with customers and on X, Microsoft explained there were actually three causes, which created a perfect storm.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week. In fact, it was the worst outage of the year, by a sizable margin. The problem took the computer giant roughly 24 hours, over the course of two business days, to get everything back up and running.

Aside from wondering when their email would be working again, the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long?

Now, we know. In a statement shared with customers and on X, Microsoft explained there were actually three causes, which created a perfect storm.

First, a bug caused servers to become unresponsive in specific conditions; second, an glitch with Microsoft Teams increased server traffic and created those conditions; and third, many additional servers were already offline from an unrelated issue.

It has been revealed that as Microsoft explained, on their own, neither issue would have caused such a large-scale problem. However, together, well, they kept one of the world's biggest tech companies scrambling for two days to fix their service.

In a social media post published on X, Microsoft's EVP of Copilot, Agents, and Platform Charles Lamanna explained the situation in detail.

According to Lamanna, a "latent defect" resulted in the company's servers becoming "overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions." The defect that caused the problem was introduced to Microsoft's systems during a July 2026 update as part of a fix for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers.

For months, as Lamanna described it, the issue went undetected, and it didn't cause any problems under normal load during Microsoft's testing process.

Sources indicate that the second problem occurred when a surge in server load set off the defect. Lamanna says that Microsoft maintains two independent network gateway systems for Microsoft 365 to handle outages and disruptions. However, 15 hours before the global Microsoft 365 outage, Teams "failed over" from the alternative networking gateway to the primary one, which supports Exchange Online. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

This wouldn't usually cause a problem, except for the latest defect introduced by the July patch.

Finally, Microsoft's servers weren't operating at 100 percent at the time. According to Lamanna, it just so happened that nearly 14 percent of the server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service "due to an unrelated problem from the previous day.".

Industry observers note that again, normally, this would have been routine maintenance. The service would still have sufficient capacity to work as normal.

All three problems occurring at once led to disaster.

"Taken together, the increased load and the reduced server capacity, caused the network gateway to encounter the latent bug from July," Lamanna writes. "This caused requests to build up until servers ultimately stopped responding. This occurred during the peak window of traffic in the United States.".

Industry observers note that recovery from the outage also took much longer than usual because servers were "immediately overwhelmed by waiting traffic and became unresponsive again." In addition, Microsoft was unable to roll back the code because the bug dated back to July. So, Microsoft essentially had to develop a patch within that short timeframe, which returned the code to its previous "good state.".

Industry observers note that the entire explanation from Microsoft is actually quite an interesting read and shows that no matter how significant the manufacturer is, massive tech concerns can still occur. Readers can check out Lamanna's entire post on X; Microsoft enterprise customers can also learn more in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

Industry observers note that microsoft has since apologized for the outage. Businesses affected by the downtime can also file a claim with the company for credits due to the downtime.

Sources indicate that apple is rolling out the second developer beta of macOS 27.3 ahead of the official launch of the revision, which includes several notable additions. Here’s what’s coming.

Two weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27.3 developer beta 1, followed by the public beta a few days later, amid a slew of hardware releases that included upcoming M6-powered iMacs and 14-inch MacBook Pro, and the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display.

Industry observers note that and contrary to macOS 27.2, the new update is shaping up to be pretty significant. In addition to expanding Siri AI support to four more languages, including Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese, the system also expands Siri AI’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing people to perform more complex actions in apps like Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders.

Sources indicate that macOS 27.3 beta 2 also introduces new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and you can read more about that here. This change comes in response to concerns about increasingly capable AI agents gaining broad access to people’ personal data and control over their Macs.

Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to create advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions, allowing the assistant to coordinate multistep actions across different apps.

Industry observers note that macOS 27.3 also introduces Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode in Safari, as well as native Live Activities support in the menu bar. Additionally, macOS 27.3 so far include native Markdown rendering in Quick Look, a new Pro Light screensaver, and additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through public iCloud links.

In a recent development, the build number for macOS 27.3 Golden Gate developer beta 2 is 26C5047e. We are digging through the system and will report back with what we find.

Sources indicate that samsung is preparing its next major update for Galaxy phones, One UI 9.5, and upcoming details have been coming to light. Here’s an overview of a lot of One UI 9.5 updates that have leaked so far.

One UI 9.5 will still be based on Android 17, but it’s set to be packed with various changes based on recent leaks. In particular, it seems like Samsung has a ton of fresh AI features in store.

Industry observers note that “Galaxy Claw” is supposedly Samsung’s latest “personal agent,” able to leverage apps on your device including your notifications, Contacts, Gmail, Messages, and more. Specifically, Android Authority reports it will be able to use Calendar, Contacts, Gallery, Gmail, Messages, Notifications, Perplexity, Phone, and Voice Recorder, with the agent able to set up scheduled tasks. It does sound like this will be a paid feature, though, with Samsung’s new $4.99/month AI Premium initiative. There would also be a new dashboard for showing AI usage.

The feature was teased during Google I/O earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that one of the less visible risks of conversational AI is its flattening effect on a culture's unique dialect and accent. Humanity speaks with a thousand voices, but assistants often just respond in a nicely generic transatlantic monotone. Now, Google is doing something about it by adding 66 regional dialects to Gemini to help it better relate to the people using it. The feature was first teased at Google I/O earlier this year, and starting today, the Android and iOS apps will be able to speak to owners in a variety of voices from different countries.

For instance, UK owners can set Gemini to speak in a Geordie, Scouse and Brummie accent to better engage with people from Tyneside, Merseyside and Birmingham. The list also includes Scots, Welsh, Northern Irish and Multicultural London English, among many others. And it's not just the UK that gets this treatment, with tailored dialects for India, Brazil, Indonesia and Korea also in the mix.

Google indicates it worked with native speakers to ensure the voices were authentic and clear, rather than exaggerated and stereotypical. It added that Gemini isn't going to suddenly fill its responses with "street slang," but instead focus on sounding more "like a local." Given how much pride people put into their accent as a signifier of their heritage, it'll be very interesting to see how well these voices are received by the people intended to use them.

It has been revealed that to activate the voices, you'll need to access the voice settings in the Gemini app or tap the three-dot menu. Google suggests a good way to test their authenticity is to ask for a recommendation for local food to better hear the "warmth and rhythm of each voice.".

The classifier flagged fewer false positives for humans to review, while getting better at identifying abusive content.

OpenAI is announcing a tool that it states will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on swiftly.

In a recent development, at a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI unveiled a classifier it states can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it’s AI-generated. It’s also offering free access to vetted organizations, giving developers more guidance on how to detect this type of content, and helping to train law enforcement on how AI can aid their investigations. The news comes as policymakers and others are pushing for more safety restrictions on AI tools, accusing OpenAI and other companies of facilitating harm to children.

Recent findings suggest that in recent years, AI-generated sexual images of children have threatened to overwhelm systems like the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) CyberTipline, which collects and triages reports of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The CyberTipline received 400,000 generative AI-related reports in 2025, an exponential increase from the 67,000 it received in 2024, and researchers have warned that the influx could make NCMEC’s workload “unmanageable.” The US government has stated that both AI-generated and non-AI-generated CSAM is illegal, and 48 states have laws to address sexually explicit AI deepfakes. But the tools to make them are widely available, and researchers say that a flood of fake images can make it harder to tell when a child is actively experiencing harm.

The influx of AI-generated CSAM reports to NCMEC is “explosive”.

In a recent development, north Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson, who cochairs the AG Alliance’s AI Task Force, stated at OpenAI’s event that the influx of AI-generated CSAM reports to NCMEC is “explosive” — and if they keep going that way, “it is going to mean that we fail in our mission.” Tech companies are facing a range of policy proposals that could require them to take more action against CSAM and other potentially harmful content for kids. The Take It Down Act now requires social media platforms to remove real or AI-generated nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours, and the newly elected Congress could seek to take stronger action against AI companies like SpaceXSI, whose Grok chatbot went on an undressing spree earlier this year. Last month eight states sued OpenAI for a separate set of alleged harms to children, citing lawsuits alleging ChatGPT encouraged illegal substance use and suicide.

OpenAI says its classifier dramatically cuts down on false positives, flagging 48 percent fewer images, while the images it did identify were twice as likely to contain abusive material. It’s designed to catch abusive AI-generated images produced by a variety of tools, including open-source models and nudifying apps. It’s also the first broadly available CSAM classifier with a specific flag for AI-generated material, said OpenAI’s head of child safety public policy, John Buckley, at the briefing. “It’s key for industry to be able to understand what images may contain a fictional child versus a real child,” Buckley added. “That triage is critical in law enforcement reporting flows.” He also emphasized, however, that laws should recognize the harm of AI-generated CSAM: “It potentially erodes social norms in offending against children, and it’s often found colocated with child sexual abuse imagery of real children,” Buckley said.

OpenAI says its classifier dramatically cuts down on false positives, flagging 48 percent fewer images.

Industry observers note that openAI’s own ChatGPT image generator is designed to deny user requests for CSAM. Now, customers who attempt to produce it will be shown a fresh warning developed with expert guidance to try to encourage them to seek help. A first offense will trigger a 24-hour pause in accessing ChatGPT and warn the user their account could be permanently closed, while offering support resources to combat the behavior. OpenAI claims it reports “all instances of CSAM” to NCMEC. In a statement, Buckley explained that the 24-hour pause is based on expert advice for best practices “and international evidence on what works to prevent and respond to CSAM seeking vs CSAM generation.” The point is “to interrupt harmful behavior and direct people toward specialist help to stop it.”.

In a recent development, jackson said that North Carolina and many other states now have laws that cover synthetic CSAM, but that partnering with a tech firm like OpenAI to help deter its creation is a fairly novel approach to an emerging issue. “Most of what AGs do is accountability work,” he told reporters at the briefing. “Most of our jurisdiction kicks in after the fact to hold people accountable for harm. But with this, we wanted to see if it was possible to develop a model of working together to prevent that harm. And I would say it’s still basically an experiment.”.

  • Huang resigned last week from Nvidia after admitting to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
  • Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman states the AI industry will be “fine” without Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the helm, even as he acknowledged the special role Huang has played in the AI boom.

Huang resigned last week from Nvidia after admitting to having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Altman made his first public comments about Huang’s departure on Monday at Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World event, where he also discussed topics ranging from data center pushback to recursive self-improvement.

Numerous executives and members of the AI industry have argued for Nvidia to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, who were among the signatories in a public letter. Many fear that Huang’s departure may cause Nvidia to rethink the enormous financial risks it has taken that have fueled the AI boom.

Huang is also reportedly setting up a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return.

When asked whether he thought Huang should return to the firm, Altman stated: “I don’t think I know enough to answer that question.”.

He expressed empathy for Huang’s situation, citing his own ousting from OpenAI in 2023 after board members accused him of withholding information.

“It’s hard to imagine what the AI revolution without Jensen and the organization he has built,” Altman noted, adding that he sees Huang as a hero, and that “heroes have flaws.”.

In a recent development, openAI and Nvidia have had a close relationship for the last decade, one that has evolved from a simple chip supplier-customer relationship into a potentially circular financing arrangement, in which Nvidia’s money helps fund purchases of its own chips. Most recently, Nvidia agreed to provide a guarantee of up to $105 billion backing OpenAI’s Ohio data center project. That’s just one of many such circular deals Nvidia has made to bankroll the AI boom while fueling demand for its own chips.

Altman said he’s not worried that the Bank of Nvidia will dry up.

Recent findings suggest that “Nvidia is, like, a behemoth of a company,” he remarked. “I think people still trust their guarantees very much.”.

Altman acknowledged the “ambition” Huang brought to the industry, the scale of which “has been quite vital.” But he didn’t go so far as to agree with the many who worry about ripple effects from Huang’s departure.

Industry observers note that “I think there’s so much demand, and it’s so clear that AI is real, and people want to use it, and the revenues and demand are growing so strongly that I think the industry will be fine,” Altman said. “But again, I think Jensen has played this extremely special and valuable role as someone to really drive things forward with great ambition.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The next wave of AI projects might just arrive in the mail.

As AI tools become more capable, people are asking chatbots to help design things they can hold, wear, or install in their homes, from custom jewelry and household gadgets to metal parts built around precise measurements.

Sources indicate that welcome to "vibe manufacturing." The phrase borrows from "vibe coding," where people describe the software they want and ask AI to help create it. Here, the goal is a physical object, with AI helping develop a design that can be printed at home or sent to a manufacturer.

Industry observers note that the appeal is easy to understand. Most people have encountered a product that would be perfect if it were a little smaller, worked differently, or fit that one awkward space. These tools offer a starting point for making their own version. Getting it right, though, still takes more than a good prompt.

In a recent development, vibe manufacturing loosely describes using conversational AI to help design and build physical things. Someone explains what they want, supplies measurements or reference images, and works with an AI tool to develop it. Depending on the project, that could involve generating a digital model, choosing components, writing software for a device, or figuring out assembly.

The bridge between the conversation and the object is often CAD, short for computer-aided design. CAD software creates precise digital designs for physical objects, and AI tools can help translate everyday requests into the code or geometry behind them.

Recent findings suggest that entrepreneur Greg Isenberg outlines the process in an Oct. 4 explainer on X. "You describe what you want. An AI turns it into a precise design file. A printer on your desk tests it overnight," he writes.

According to recent reports, tools such as the open-source text-to-cad project support that process, providing workflows for creating models with AI agents, producing engineering drawings, and checking designs for fabrication. The resulting files can go to a printer or an outside shop with the equipment to make the parts.

Some of the projects getting attention solve problems that are deeply specific to their creators.

It has been revealed that in October, entrepreneur and former X head of product Nikita Bier posted that he'd used AI to design a dog door with a Wi-Fi-controlled lock, customized to his house. Despite having no background in metal fabrication or electrical engineering, he said it was being manufactured for almost the same price as a mass-produced alternative. "We are now entering into an era where any product can be created exactly to a consumer's preferences & needs," he wrote.

Other makers are tackling repairs. In a post on r/ApolloScooters, one Reddit user described using Claude to modify an existing design file after their scooter’s rear fender broke. They ordered a replacement through a 3D-printing service and shared a photo of the result, while noting that they would make the next version shorter.

Industry observers note that around the house, customization can be decorative, too. An employee for AI modeling tool Meshy, Jessica Bergau, used the manufacturer's AI tool to design cabinet knobs, then asked Claude to generate a script that added screw threads to the models. A blog post documents her plastic prints and the work needed to get an actual screw to fit. Sources indicate that some people are taking their AI-generated ideas to professional craftspeople. In an Instagram post, Dubai-based jeweler AV Creations mentioned a client brought in an AI-generated design that its team recreated as a bespoke gold dog tag pendant, complete with geometric engravings, diamond detailing, and a sculptural carved cube.

Others are experimenting with more complex systems. In a post on X, Ruben Kostandyan shared that he'd asked GPT-5.5 to design an industrial mini HVAC system using ForgeCAD.

Industry observers note that and some projects start with wanting a device that doesn't quite exist on store shelves. In a recent Business Insider report, David Plakon described using AI to help build a homemade answering box so his children could leave messages for their grandparents.

The report also featured a sheet-metal robot arm and a custom steel component for securing a camper to a truck.

It has been revealed that greg Isenberg sees a business opportunity in what he calls "the gadgets nobody would build" — products for audiences too small to interest a large manufacturer. He points to accessories for particular bikes or coffee machines, replacement parts for discontinued products, and equipment tailored to an individual business.

"When the design is a file and the factory makes one at a time, the product can fit you instead," he writes.

Recent findings suggest that that vision extends beyond personal projects to businesses serving small markets. Whether those businesses can consistently deliver reliable products at a workable price is a separate question.

Turning an AI-assisted design into a physical object often relies on existing manufacturing services: SendCutSend lets customers order custom metal parts, Xometry offers processes including machining and 3D printing, and JLCPCB can manufacture and assemble circuit boards. Each requires files specifying what to build.

But access to production equipment doesn’t guarantee a workable design. "A design can look perfect on screen and be impossible to manufacture," Isenberg writes. He recommends checking a manufacturer’s guidelines, testing a physical prototype, and paying a mechanical engineer to review files before ordering.

Recent findings suggest that dominic Böttger's account of making a case for an air-quality sensor shows why. He used Claude Code to develop the enclosure, but early versions had misplaced supports and an opening wide enough for the circuit board to slide out. Getting it right took seven design revisions and three prints, with photographs helping guide corrections. "The feedback loop needs the physical part," he writes.

Industrial manufacturers face the added challenge of making those results repeatable. Technology and manufacturing organization Automation Alley explores that ambition in its March 2026 Integr8 playbook, Vibe Manufacturing: Where AI Meets Additive. Engineers set requirements such as strength, durability, and cost, then use AI to explore designs for additive manufacturing, the category that includes 3D printing.

It has been revealed that "AI explores the options. Additive manufacturing turns those options into physical reality," CEO Tom Kelly writes in the foreword. The report also discusses "Smart Product Recipes," digital instructions intended to standardize production across locations.

As AI tools improve, more people may get the chance to make the products they've been wishing someone would sell. The real test will be how well those ideas hold up once they leave the chat window.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the heels of the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration is preparing to crack down on foreign data centers that are fueling China’s advancements in artificial intelligence by allowing remote access to otherwise restricted high-end chips necessary for AI training.

In a summary of the rule change, the Commerce Department noted it was closing a loophole that previously allowed foreign rivals like China, Russia, and Iran to bypass export curbs on certain advanced computer chips by instead renting access to those chips from data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.

Sources indicate that US rivals could possibly use that access to train and run advanced AI models “capable of supporting military- and intelligence-related activities that could threaten US national security or foreign policy interests,” the Commerce Department stated. Among threats, the US fears rivals could use advanced AI to develop “more effective weapons of mass destruction and advanced conventional weapons, coordinated cyber-espionage and targeted cyber-disruption, algorithmic theft, and weaponized disinformation.”.

Now, the rules have been tightened up so much that the South China Morning Post reported that, “as a result, any advanced chips made for a Chinese firm are assumed to be restricted, and factories must ask the US government for a license before shipping them.”.

Sources indicate that the rule change takes effect 90 days after it’s posted to the Federal Register. Moving forward, companies headquartered in any of those countries deemed to “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion” to China, Russia, and Iran must apply for a license with strict know-your-customer controls when transferring high volumes of advanced chips. If a license is granted, companies will have to “perform robust due diligence,” submitting monthly reports on transactions that thoroughly detail all parties involved, as well as their parent companies, and the final destination for chips sold.

In a press release Sunday, the Commerce Department described the rule change as “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.” An exception was carved out for companies providing computing power “exclusively used for commercial recommender systems.” The Department remarked it was acting to “prevent certain foreign actors from leveraging advanced computing power based on US technology to threaten US national security and foreign policy interests.”.

Without the intervention, officials fear that China could develop a military or economic edge, The New York Times reported.

It has been revealed that nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after admitting to an affair with a woman, Alice Huang, suspected of serving as a Chinese spy. Congress is probing if Alice Huang used her personal relationship with Jensen Huang to help her former firm, Megaspeed, become one of Nvidia’s biggest customers, then used that position to smuggle Nvidia’s restricted AI chips into China. China has denied that Alice Huang was a spy, and Megaspeed has denied that smuggling occurred, while launching its own internal probe.

Megaspeed is a Singaporean data center firm whose primary business is cloud computing and AI infrastructure. Prior to the rule change, selling remote access to AI servers to customers in China was perfectly legal, NYT noted. But now, the Commerce Department has given firms like Megaspeed 90 days to either obtain licenses or face future export restrictions.

Whether or not to add more chip curbs has been a polarizing debate in the Trump administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reportedly butted heads with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. When the Megaspeed news broke, Bessent pushed for curbs, but Lutnick reportedly appeared “too cozy” with Nvidia to move. Instead, Lutnick initially favored looser controls that Nvidia claimed would ensure global dominance of US technology. (A Commerce Department spokesperson told NYT that Bessent has never confronted Lutnick over his handling of Megaspeed.).

In a recent development, any companies found violating the rules could face a “range of consequences,” the Commerce Department stated after reportedly bending to Bessent’s pressure campaign. Those include possibly facing latest import restrictions, stricter license requirements, downgrading their status in the US export control regime, or other changes to their firm’s or their base country’s entity-list designations.

Although the summary of the rule change stated that “Commerce will be actively monitoring for countries that tolerate evasion” of the anti-diversion policy, it’s unclear how aggressively the Commerce Department might enforce the rule, NYT noted.

Bessent has publicly criticized Lutnick for failing to sanction Megaspeed, and NYT reported that ultimately, enforcement of the stricter rules—which Bessent helped draft—“would be up to the Commerce Department.”.

According to recent reports, “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?” Bessent said on a CNBC appearance. “I think it’s important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that.”.

Industry observers note that there’s even a push to oust Lutnick over his position on chips, but The Guardian reported that Donald Trump confirmed he has no aims to replace the AI industry-friendly commerce secretary. On Monday, Trump told reporters that Lutnick was right to delay blacklisting Megaspeed, because “if you didn’t delay it… you could have a blow-up with China.”.

Sources indicate that at the press gaggle, Trump aligned with China in saying that there’s no evidence yet that Alice Huang was a spy. He also joined a band of prominent tech leaders calling for Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, saying that it wasn’t a “bad idea.”.

In a recent development, “Nobody’s proven that she’s a spy,” Trump stated. “She may not be a spy.”.

However, US investigators have alleged that they found “Alice Huang used industry contacts and a series of shell companies to access 240,000 chips banned for export into China,” CBS News reported.

China is unlikely to welcome the newly introduced rules, as it has consistently accused the US of fabricating the spying claims to justify imposing additional chip restrictions.

However, a senior Trump official, granted anonymity to discuss sensitive policy matters, told the NYT that Trump “did not expect countermeasures from China in response.”.

Industry observers note that trump will be in China for an economic summit this week, including a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The fresh curbs could potentially disrupt those talks, according to Hong Yuan, a researcher and secretary-general of the Center for American Military Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Hong told the People’s Daily that China will likely view the rule change as politically motivated.

In a recent development, “Before any judicial causality was established, Washington handed down a political conviction, substituting suspicion for proof, espionage for personal contact, and an industrial embargo for private conduct,” Hong said. “The issue is not the cause of tighter controls, but a political catalyst.”.

Industry observers note that the upcoming policy could hurt the US, experts told the Chinese outlets. Analysts told the South China Morning Post that the policy could “accelerate Chinese companies’ shift to domestic AI chips.” Other experts told the People’s Daily—which is the official newspaper of the Chinese Communist Party—that “the cost of switching back to US platforms will rise” over time. If that happened, it could potentially lock in Chinese technology over America’s in “the world’s largest single consumer market for chips,” experts stated.

Sun Chenghao, senior fellow at the Center for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University in Beijing, told the People’s Daily that “what US companies stand to lose could be customers and technological influence for years to come.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dust off that Hitachi and put your Slack on “Do not disturb,” because AO3 is back online, baby.

After weeks off the internet due to an unspecified security incident, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit that runs the hugely popular fan fiction forum, unveiled on November 15 that service had been restored.

Industry observers note that “We understand that the wait and uncertainty surrounding AO3’s return have been difficult, and we apologize for the inconvenience,” the statement reads. “We greatly appreciate your support during the downtime, and continued patience as our volunteers work hard to return AO3 to its full functionality.”.

The news came as a pleasant surprise to AO3’s devoted fans, as the website had revealed in late October that restoring service could take between two to four weeks. To that end, the OTW statement indicates that some of the site’s features, such as user icons and external work importing, have been temporarily disabled in order to expedite the site’s return. It also warned that users “may experience a delay before AO3 loads,” due to “high traffic.”.

In a recent development, founded in 2007, AO3 is one of the most popular fan fiction forums on the internet, boasting more than 11 million owners and over 18 million original works. Following its temporary shutdown, many devastated fans started sharing Google Docs of their favorite fanfics, sparking some concerns among authors worried about AI scraping and their work being posted to other websites without their permission. Others resorted to other platforms to get their Dramione or Hollanov fix, such as Tumblr, which reported a 75 percent jump in upcoming sign-ups among users between the ages of 18 and 25, according to data shared with WIRED.

Throughout the 17-day shutdown, AO3 has remained vague about the causes of the security breach. In its statement announcing its return, OTW said that while it has “no reason to believe that the user database was compromised,” it can’t rule out the possibility; the website recommends customers change their passwords “as a precaution.” The site is also pairing with a security firm “to help prevent future incidents.”.

Though the suggestion prompted some concern on social media, for the most part fans are jubilant about the end of the “AO3 apocalypse,” as some have referred to the shutdown.

It has been revealed that “Ao3 returned on a Sunday,” one fan wrote in a tweet that has 1.2 million views. “Just like Jesus.”.

The simple and convenient Apple Maps feature every CarPlay user should know about

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let your friends know what time you'll be arriving.
  • For many iPhone customers, Apple CarPlay has become synonymous with a quality driving experience, from playing their favorite tunes to navigating to their next destination.
  • Recent findings suggest that I am, of course, referring to sharing your estimated time of arrival (ETA) through Apple Maps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let your friends know what time you'll be arriving.

For many iPhone customers, Apple CarPlay has become synonymous with a quality driving experience, from playing their favorite tunes to navigating to their next destination. And although Apple continues to upgrade its popular infotainment system, one of its most useful features has been hidden in Apple Maps for years and is critical to letting your family, friends, and, if you are like me, enemies know when you will arrive at your destination.

Recent findings suggest that I am, of course, referring to sharing your estimated time of arrival (ETA) through Apple Maps. Most consumers are probably familiar with Apple's Find My and location-sharing functions, but CarPlay's Share ETA feature is woefully underappreciated. Both simple to use and highly customizable, the feature is a godsend for worried parents and surprise parties everywhere.

Industry observers note that to enable Share ETA, go to Settings > Apps > Maps. From here, scroll down to Share ETA and enable the feature. You can also enable location sharing in Messages, Contacts and Find My. You may also want to turn on Siri to make sharing an ETA more convenient. To do so, go to your iPhone's Settings, tap Siri and enable Turn on Siri.

Sharing your ETA is a simple way to improve your CarPlay experience. If you're using Siri, you can initiate a voice command when you're following Maps directions, either by holding the voice command button on your steering wheel or saying "Hey Siri" if your car supports voice activation. Next, say "share my ETA with (contact name).".

It has been revealed that if you would rather not use Apple's voice assistant, you can share your ETA directly in Maps. After you've set off, tap the route card at the bottom of the screen, then Share ETA and choose a recipient. If the contact isn't on the list, you can find them under Open Contacts. To share with more than one person, tap Sharing with at the bottom of the screen, Open Contacts and select your intended recipients. You can also stop sharing your ETA by opening the route card again, tapping Sharing with, selecting Stop Sharing ETA and choosing the contact you want to stop sharing with.

You can also automatically share your ETA with someone by adding their contact to a pinned location. First, go to Maps > Places > Pinned. Next, tap the blue information button > Add Person. Next, tap the desired contact and confirm the selection. Now, whenever you select the pinned location in Apple Maps and tap Go, it will automatically share your ETA.

  • For instance, you can ask about your recent step count or heart rate readings, find out about activity rings progress, log medications and more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Siri AI expanded on what kinds of things you can ask Apple’s voice assistant in many ways, one area where the system took a step back was health data. Since Siri AI’s launch in iOS 27.0, the system has enforced guardrails that do not allow it to access data from the Health app, despite the older Siri Classic being able to do just that.

In a recent development, however, it seems Apple is about to close the gap. In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, just released to developers today, people are now able to ask their iPhone about health data related questions and Siri AI will answer.

For instance, you can ask about your recent step count or heart rate readings, find out about activity rings progress, log medications and more.

When asking Siri for health stats, the assistant generates a human natural language response and renders a little inline card that uses familiar user interface elements from the Health app. Similarly, if you ask about your activity rings, a visualisation of your activity rings is shown in the chat transcript.

Again, this is catch-up compared to what you’ve been able to do with old Siri for several years at this point. However, empowered by the LLM behind the scenes, you can ask questions about your health data that are a bit more open-ended.

According to recent reports, you can also do more complicated requests like ‘Send a message to Chance about the status of my activity rings’, or ‘How many steps am I on track to do this week?’. These are the kind of tasks that old Siri would never be able to do.

At least on this current build, the upcoming Siri AI Health functionality appears to have been enabled on iOS. It’s right now unclear if the functionality will also be available through watchOS.

iOS 27.3 also introduces a revamped Health app, with a radically new design that includes new insights, suggestions and views about your health and fitness.

iOS 27.3 is right now in beta and is expected to be released publicly later this year, likely in early December.

In a recent development, we’re only a couple of months away from our next Galaxy Unpacked, and while the expanded Galaxy S27 series is practically guaranteed to show up, the real fun tends to lie in whatever other gadgets show up alongside Samsung’s next flagship smartphone release. Based on some newly introduced leaks, it’s sure looking like the next mobile accessory on the company’s docket is a return to over-ear wireless headphones, and so far, they’re sounding pretty promising.

Samsung hasn’t produced over-ear headphones in about a decade — under its own name, at least — but it looks like that’s about to change. We hadn’t heard much in the way of details on the organization’s next audio release, rumored to be named ‘Galaxy Studio,’ but a fresh leak courtesy of SamMobile is finally changing that. We’ll have to keep waiting for full renders, but these leaked graphics are giving us a general idea of what they might look like, plus a couple of key features.

Unsurprisingly, Galaxy Studio will include ANC, complete with a dedicated button to toggle the setting between its usual modes. Volume controls also could come in the shape of physical buttons, but playback controls appear to be relegated to a touch-sensitive area on its earpads, something that’s become relatively standard among the flagship headphone competition. SamMobile also reports it’ll come in “at least” black and red colorways, while a leak from earlier this month suggested rotational earcups.

According to recent reports, again, I don’t want to read too much into these leaked graphics, as it’s always possible the final release has a handful of changes. Based on these images, though, I’m pleasantly surprised to see Samsung avoiding an attempt at copying Apple’s AirPods Max design. The larger cups, combined with their ability to twist and turn for easy storage, sounds much closer to most (but not all) of Sony’s over-ear efforts across the last decade or so, and when it comes to headphones, there are much, much worse choices you could look to for inspiration. If Samsung can hit the right price on these — or bundle them with one of their ever-more-expensive smartphones — they could be a real winner.

Frequent consumers of some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features will require an iCloud Plus subscription to avoid limits.﻿.

Frequent people of some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features will require an iCloud Plus subscription to avoid limits.﻿.

Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the enhancement to test newly introduced per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.

Sources indicate that basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.

Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The organization reportedly aims to provide notifications when owners are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.

It has been revealed that instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus prepares (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price. The $2.99/month 200GB subscription includes 2x the usage, the $9.99/month 2TB proposal includes 5x the usage, while the $29.99/month 6TB and $59.99 12TB/month options bump the usage limit to 10x and 20x, respectively. Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.

Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

Tesla goes all-in on the Cybercab with upcoming €3B Berlin Gigafactory expansion

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just two months after putting its first Cybercabs on the road, Tesla is making a multibillion-dollar bet on mass production of the golden-hued, two-seat autonomous vehicles.
  • Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer declared Monday that it will spend €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its Berlin gigafactory, with aims to begin building Cybercabs there in 2029.
  • According to recent reports, construction is expected to begin in the first half of 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just two months after putting its first Cybercabs on the road, Tesla is making a multibillion-dollar bet on mass production of the golden-hued, two-seat autonomous vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer declared Monday that it will spend €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its Berlin gigafactory, with aims to begin building Cybercabs there in 2029. The newly introduced building in Grünheide, just east of Berlin, will be capable of producing up to 1 million vehicles per year, André Thierig, Tesla’s senior director of manufacturing for the site, wrote on LinkedIn.

According to recent reports, construction is expected to begin in the first half of 2027. The expansion will make the facility the most technologically advanced of all Tesla factories, Thierig added.

Tesla has been directing more resources toward the Cybercab project, a reflection of its mission to become an AI and robotics organization, rather than just an automaker.

The manufacturer has already declared looks to cease production of the Cybertruck next year, in part to make room for Cybercab manufacturing at its factory in Austin, Texas.

According to recent reports, musk doesn’t see much of a future for drive-it-yourself EVs even though demand for the Model 3 and Model Y has remained strong despite flagging U.S. sales. The company delivered more than 486,000 vehicles in the third quarter, about 6,000 more than the second quarter. Sales in Europe have been rising as EV adoption continues apace.

Musk has been far more interested in pushing the organization toward fully automated driving systems that don’t require a human driver to pay attention — unlike the company’s current advanced driver assistance system, known as Full Self-Driving (Supervised).

The steering wheel-free Cybercab, which was first revealed in 2024 and launched publicly in September, is the current centerpiece of that plan. It’s notable not just for its lack of a steering wheel, pedals, and other traditional motor vehicle equipment, some of which is required under federal safety standards. (Federal regulators are presently investigating Tesla’s self-certification of the vehicle.).

Sources indicate that tesla’s approach to self-driving systems differs from that of competitors such as Waymo. Tesla relies solely on cameras, rather than additional other sensors such as lidar, to help its self-driving system the means to understand its environment. Camera data mimics human vision, but without sufficient training, AI models can struggle to interpret situations that additional sensor data might help clarify.

Sources indicate that tesla has so far taken a slow approach to its Cybercab rollout. The vehicles have been restricted from driving late at night, though Tesla has been working to extend their operating hours. In the more than two months that Cybercabs have been operating, they haven’t had any major incidents.

According to recent reports, that track record appears to have given Tesla enough confidence to commit significant resources to expanding Cybercab production and availability. Tesla has about 1,307 robotaxis registered in Texas. Most are modified Model Y vehicles that are used in robotaxi services in several Texas cities. But the Cybercab numbers are growing with about 573 on roads in Austin and soon Dallas.

Now, Europe is firmly on its roadmap, too.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond in the upcoming film from director Denis Villeneuve.
  • Pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role.
  • Recent findings suggest that "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond in the upcoming film from director Denis Villeneuve. It will be the 26th James Bond film and the first since Amazon MGM took over the iconic franchise.

Pattinson will be the seventh actor to play the role. Monday's announcement — which came in part via an Instagram post — ends a long period of speculation about who would take over as "007" after Daniel Craig.

Recent findings suggest that "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime," Pattinson said in a statement. "I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.".

According to recent reports, pattinson has appeared in several big-ticket films this year, including Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" and psychological thriller "Primetime," and he'll soon appear in "Dune: Part Three," also directed by Villeneuve. Pattinson, who rose to fame with the Twilight movie series, is also in production for Matt Reeves' "The Batman Part II," a follow-up to the 2022 film based on the DC comic.

The upcoming Bond film will have a script by Steven Knight and will be produced by Amy Pascal, known for her work on the Spider-Man franchise, and David Heyman, who produced all eight Harry Potter films.

Industry observers note that "We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007," Villeneuve said. "I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our newly introduced James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.".

Sources indicate that in 2022, Amazon bought MGM Studios, which had long produced the Bond movies, for roughly $8.45 billion. Amazon MGM then acquired creative control of the James Bond intellectual property rights in 2025, when it closed a deal with longtime producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson.

The film is still untitled, and Amazon MGM hasn't declared a projected release date.

#558. Industry News: Meet the fresh James Bond: Robert Pattinson

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Meet the fresh James Bond: Robert Pattinson

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Internet has been abuzz for months about which actor would replace Daniel Craig as British agent 007 James Bond in the franchise.
  • “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement.
  • The choice will reunite Pattinson with Denis Villeneuve, who recently worked with him on the forthcoming Dune: Part III and will direct the next (as yet untitled) Bond installment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Internet has been abuzz for months about which actor would replace Daniel Craig as British agent 007 James Bond in the franchise. We finally have the answer: Robert Pattinson, who built on his 2005 role as the doomed Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire into an illustrious career mixing roles in franchises and Hollywood blockbusters with daring arthouse fare.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson said in a statement. “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”.

The choice will reunite Pattinson with Denis Villeneuve, who recently worked with him on the forthcoming Dune: Part III and will direct the next (as yet untitled) Bond installment. “I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” Villeneuve remarked in a statement. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our fresh James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”.

Not everyone is happy with the casting choice; some have never forgiven Pattinson for the Twilight franchise, despite the actor’s impressive recent films. Pattinson has played darker roles in recent years, often as a villain. And at 40, Pattinson is a bit older than the actors he beat out, most notably Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden (Slow Horses), Josh O’Connor (Wake Up, Dead Man), and Callum Turner (Fantastic Beasts).

But Pattinson is a logical choice for Bond; heck, he’s already played a secret agent in Christopher Nolan’s Tenet (2020). In fact, he originally topped the list of longtime Bond franchise steward Barbara Broccoli’s and Michael G. Wilson’s choices to take over from Craig. They shelved that idea when Pattinson was cast in Matt Reeves’ The Batman. But Broccoli and Wilson no longer have creative control over Bond, having sold the rights to Amazon MGM for $20 million.

Pattinson’s box office record this year probably didn’t hurt either: He played central roles in The Drama, Primetime, and The Odyssey, all of which made back their production costs and then some, with Dune: Part III still to come. It’s unclear how his Bond commitments will affect Pattinson’s future as Batman; The Batman: Part 2 has faced production delays (and a director change) and is slated for a 2028 release. Should there be a third installment—not assured in the wake of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s departure from DC Studios—Reeves will likely work around Pattinson’s Bond schedule.

“James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies,” producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman mentioned in a statement. “The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times.”.

Breaking: Why scammers try to keep you on the phone (and how to spot their tactics)

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If something feels off, hang up and call the organization back on their official number.
  • That unexpected call from someone claiming to be from your bank can be worrisome, especially if they're calling to alert you about a suspicious money transfer.
  • But more than the emergency itself, their instruction to stay on call is the real catch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If something feels off, hang up and call the organization back on their official number.

That unexpected call from someone claiming to be from your bank can be worrisome, especially if they're calling to alert you about a suspicious money transfer. Your savings are at risk, but fret not, the caller who somehow got hold of your number says they can stop it — as long as you stay on the line.

But more than the emergency itself, their instruction to stay on call is the real catch. Scammers are counting on you to not hang up, as that valuable time helps them earn your trust. It then leads to turning up the pressure, which eventually leads you toward a decision you otherwise wouldn't take. That's when they might ask for a verification code, or straight up ask you to make a transfer. Keeping you occupied just long enough is the blueprint, so you don't end up calling the bank for a second opinion.

It has been revealed that dedicated scammers are known to stay on the line as the victims login to the accounts to transfer funds, buy gift cards or make a visit to the nearby ATM to withdraw cash. Some even go as far as to school you on what to tell bank employees when questioned about that odd transaction. When the person "helping" you protect your savings is deterring you from speaking to anyone else, that's a pretty obvious sign that something is off.

It has been revealed that one possible way in could be a compromised bank account. A creative scammer could inform you about open accounts under your name or even scare you with an arrest warrant. The plan is to make you feel that following their instructions is the only way out, so hanging up doesn't feel like a plausible option.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes, the whole script includes more than just one scam artist. Back in August 2026, the FBI reported that scammers posing as bank employees told their victims that their information had been used to open an account to purchase illegal firearms. The scammers then transferred the victims to someone posing as an FBI agent, but disconnected after the victims were encouraged to verify the number.

Shortly after, they received a call displaying the FBI's Boston office number, which had been spoofed. These "FBI agents" could then ask the victims to continue the conversations using an encrypted messaging app. The FBI didn't specify how many people were targeted by this scheme.

It has been revealed that but the threatening villain persona is not the only way these scammers are out to get you. Some of them act professional, stay patient and even go a step further to sound sympathetic. Now, when these friendly voices start to discourage you from reaching out to the organization directly or getting a second opinion, that should get your alarm bells ringing. After all, con artists don't want all of their efforts to result in failure.

Once the small talk is done, call handlers may switch to a dictating tone in order to get the outcome they want. This is a clear warning sign. When the caller demands you stay connected or instructs you to keep the conversation private, be sure to trust your instincts and end the call.

When they ask you to move funds to a "safer" account, it's time to hang up. Any request for passwords or even one-time verification codes should also be met with a call termination. Since scammers are often savvy enough to spoof authentic phone numbers, caller ID isn't all that reliable either.

Industry observers note that once you hang up or end that text conversation, reach out to the organization, but only using its official app or the number on your bank card or statement. Steer clear of contact numbers that the caller gives you, and trusting the customer-service numbers from sponsored search results isn't safe either. If it's a bit late to heed this advice and you've already shared sensitive information or worse transferred money to the scammer, contact your bank or payment provider right away.

It has been revealed that did you know your phone can filter out some of these unwanted calls? On iPhones running iOS 26 or newer, head to Settings > Apps > Phone > Screen Unknown Callers to enable extra incoming call checks, which include silencing unsaved numbers or asking callers to state who they are before they're connected.

Sources indicate that if you own a supported Samsung Galaxy phone, try out spam filtering under Phone > Settings > Caller ID and spam protection, and Google Pixel owners can set up Call Screen using the Phone app's settings on supported devices in eligible regions. The downside is that legitimate callers can sometimes get caught by these filters.

According to recent reports, companies like Meta, Microsoft and Starlink have already worked to help take down over a million scam accounts. If you want to help save other unsuspecting consumers, it's best to report suspected scams to the FTC.

  • First up, it appears that Google Messages is getting some voice note improvements, as spotted by Android Authority in one of its recent APK teardowns.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Messages always has something going on, be it a UI update or the addition of a fresh feature - and the messaging service could be rolling out not one, but two handy tools soon.

First up, it appears that Google Messages is getting some voice note improvements, as spotted by Android Authority in one of its recent APK teardowns.

Sources indicate that sick and tired of voice note playback stopping when you leave a chat? Google is fixing this.

In a recent development, at the moment, you can listen to voice notes and audio files when you switch to a different app, but it stops when you leave a chat and return to the main conversation list. Although it's not live yet, Android Authority claims it managed to enable a feature, which it notes allows audio playback to continue even when exiting a chat. This finally deals with a huge pain point, allowing you to listen to a voice note from one person when replying to another in a separate conversation.

It has been revealed that this is the biggest upgrade when it comes to voice notes and audio files, but it's not the only one Google is working on. Additionally, the outlet spotted new playback control buttons in the notification center, including new pause, play, and forward icons supporting 5- to 30-second skip and rewind.

As far as aesthetics go, Google is tipped to roll out small but noticeable changes for icons within chats. If the new features roll out, the voice note icon could change from its current wave-like symbol to a standard microphone, which makes more sense, though I can see it being mistaken for a speech-to-text function.

When you have friends and family constantly on your case, organizing your conversations can make a huge difference, but Google Messages' six-pin limit just isn't enough to suffice for some users. Thankfully, this could soon be a thing of the past.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Android Authority carried out another deep dive into Google Messages' latest beta, finding strings that point to the possibility of Google lifting its long-time pin restrictions as well as reviving its old chat pins layout.

Depending on how many chats you pin, the layout will switch based on this number. If you pin six chats or fewer, your conversations will appear in the current tile-based design. If you pin more than six, your chats will automatically switch to the app's previous list-based layout, which allowed you to pin up to 20 different conversations - though we don't know if that number will be reinstated for this patch; the strings in Android Authority's findings don't clarify that.

It has been revealed that as it is with every teardown, it's not guaranteed that the features in development will see the light of day. There's always the chance that Google could abandon the ideas altogether. That remarked, if the upgrades remain on Google's release calendar, there's no doubt they'd be welcomed quality-of-life upgrades for those who rely on Google Messages to stay connected.
